title: Buttons
summary: Bootstrap button classes add a shape, colour and spacing to a button or link.
introduction: Bootstrap button classes add a shape, colour and spacing to a button or link. Pick a main button and a quieter second button. Use a button for an action and a link for going to an address.
learningObjectives: Apply btn with a colour or outline variant to buttons, links and inputs
Change a button's size and make it fill its container
Disable buttons and links in a way that works for keyboard and screen reader users
Combine buttons in button groups and toolbars

blocks.text: The btn class and its variants

`.btn` gives an element the shape of a button: `.375rem .75rem` padding, a 1px border, `.375rem` rounded corners, a 1rem font and no underline. On its own it is transparent. The **variant** class, one of `btn-primary`, `btn-secondary`, `btn-success`, `btn-danger`, `btn-warning`, `btn-info`, `btn-light`, `btn-dark` or `btn-link`, supplies the background, border and text colours, including their hover, focus and active shades. The classes work identically on `<button>`, `<a>` and `<input type="submit">`.

blocks.text: Warning, info and light use black text because white would not meet the contrast ratio on those bright backgrounds; Bootstrap picks the text colour automatically for each variant. Always give a `<button>` an explicit `type`: inside a `<form>` the default is `submit`, so a button meant to open a dialog would also submit the form.

Replace `btn-*` with `btn-outline-*` for a lighter look: transparent background, coloured border and coloured text, which fill with the solid colour on hover. Outline buttons suit secondary actions placed next to a solid primary one.

blocks.title: Primary action with an outlined alternative
blocks.code:
<button type="button" class="btn btn-primary">Save changes</button>
<button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-secondary">Cancel</button>
<button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-danger">Delete</button>

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
Save changes: solid blue button with white text
Cancel: transparent button with a grey border and grey text; on hover it becomes solid grey with white text
Delete: transparent button with a red border and red text; on hover it becomes solid red with white text

blocks.text: `btn-lg` enlarges the padding to `.5rem 1rem` and the font to 1.25rem; `btn-sm` shrinks them to `.25rem .5rem` and .875rem. Buttons are `inline-block`, so to stretch one across its container either add `w-100` or wrap a stack of buttons in `d-grid gap-2`, which also spaces them evenly.

blocks.text: A `<button>` is disabled with the native `disabled` attribute: it turns 65% opaque, ignores the pointer and leaves the tab order. Links have no `disabled` attribute, so a link styled as a button needs three things: the `.disabled` class for the look, `aria-disabled="true"` so assistive technology announces the state, and `tabindex="-1"` to remove it from the tab order. `.active` with `aria-pressed="true"` shows a button as pressed, which is what the toggle behaviour `data-bs-toggle="button"` switches on and off when the JavaScript bundle is loaded.

blocks.title: Common mistake: a variant without the base class
blocks.text: `class="btn-primary"` on its own renders a plain, unstyled browser button. Since Bootstrap 5.2 the variant classes only *define* CSS variables such as `--bs-btn-bg`; it is `.btn` that actually uses them. The same applies to outlines and sizes: `btn-outline-danger` and `btn-lg` do nothing without `btn` beside them. When a button looks wrong, check that the base class is present before anything else.

`.btn-group` joins a series of buttons into one bar: the inner borders overlap and only the outer corners stay rounded. Give the group `role="group"` and an `aria-label` so screen readers describe it as one control. `.btn-group-vertical` stacks the buttons, `.btn-group-lg` and `.btn-group-sm` resize the whole group, and `.btn-toolbar` lines several groups up with spacing between them.

Rendered result
blocks.content:
Day / Week / Month: one joined bar with a single blue outline; Day is filled solid blue (active), the others are transparent with blue text
Below it, two small grey bars, "Cut Copy Paste" and "Undo Redo", 8px apart; within each bar the buttons share borders and only the outer corners are rounded

blocks.title: Links versus buttons
blocks.text: Use `<a class="btn">` when the action navigates to another page and `<button>` when it does something on the current page (opens a dialog, submits, toggles). When a link must act like a button, add `role="button"` so assistive technology announces it correctly.

questions.question: Which variant renders black text instead of white?
questions.explanation: warning, info and light have bright backgrounds, so Bootstrap gives them black text to keep enough contrast. primary, success, danger, secondary and dark use white text.

questions.question: Adding the `disabled` attribute to `<a class="btn btn-primary">` disables the link.
questions.explanation: Links do not support the disabled attribute. Use the .disabled class together with aria-disabled="true" and tabindex="-1".
